text:
A dice is thrown two times and the sum of the
scores appearing on the die is observed to be
a multiple of 4. Then the conditional probability
that the score 4 has appeared atleast once is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let A is the event for getting score a multiple
of 4.

So, A = { (1, 3), (3, 1), (2, 2), (2, 6), (6, 2),
(3, 5), (5, 3), (4, 4), (6, 6) } = 09

n(A) = 9

B : Score of 4 has appeared at least once.

B = {(4, 4)}

So, Required probability = $\frac{1}{9}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
The lines

$\vec{r}=\left (\hat{i}-\hat{j}\right )+l\left (2\hat{i}+\widehat{k}\right )$ and 

$\vec{r}=\left (2\hat{i}-\hat{j}\right )+m\left (\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\widehat{k}\right )$
options: do not intersect for any values of $l$ and m
intersect for all values of $l$ and m
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A general point of the first line is $(1+2l,-1,l)$ and of the second line is $(2+m,-1+m,m)$.

At a common point the coordinates agree:

$1+2l=2+m,-1=-1+m,l=m$

The second equation gives $m=0$, and the third then gives $l=0$.

With these values $1+2l=1$ while $2+m=2$, so the first equation fails. The three equations have no common solution, so the lines do not intersect for any values of $l$ and $m$ (their directions $2\hat{i}+\hat{k}$ and $\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ are not parallel, so the lines are skew).

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
A hyperbola having the transverse axis of
length
$\sqrt{2}$ has the same foci as that of the ellipse
$3x^{2} + 4y^{2} = 12$, then this hyperbola does not
pass through which of the following points?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Ellipse : $\frac{x^{2}}{4}+\frac{y^{2}}{3}=1$

eccentricity = $\sqrt{1-\frac{3}{4}}=\frac{1}{2}$

$\therefore$ foci = ($\pm$ 1, 0)

for hyperbola, given $2a=\sqrt{2}\Rightarrow a=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\therefore$ hyperbola will be

$\frac{x^{2}}{1/2}-\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$

eccentricity = $\sqrt{1+2b^{2}}$

$\therefore$ foci $=\left (\pm \sqrt{\frac{1+2b^{2}}{2}},0\right )$

$\because$ Ellipse and hyperbola have same foci

$\Rightarrow \sqrt{\frac{1+2b^{2}}{2}}=1$

$\Rightarrow b^{2}=\frac{1}{2}$

$\therefore$ Equation of hyperbola : $\frac{x^{2}}{1/2}-\frac{y^{2}}{1/2}=1$

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{2}-y^{2}=\frac{1}{2}$

Clearly $\left (\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}},\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )$ does not lie on it.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
If the first term of an A.P. is 3 and the sum of
its first 25 terms is equal to the sum of its next
15 terms, then the common difference of this
A.P. is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
First 25 terms = a, a + d, .......,a + 24d

Next 15 terms = a + 25d, a + 26d, ......, a + 39d

$\therefore$ $\frac{25}{2}[2a+24d]=\frac{15}{2}[2(a+25d)+14d]$

$\Rightarrow$ 50a + 600d = 15 [2a + 50d + 14d]

$\Rightarrow$ 20a + 600d = 960d

$\Rightarrow$ 60 = 360d

$\Rightarrow$ d = $\frac{1}{6}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
Let P be a point on the parabola, $y^{2}$
 = 12x and
N be the foot of the perpendicular drawn from
P on the axis of the parabola. A line is now
drawn through the mid-point M of PN, parallel
to its axis which meets the parabola at Q. If the
y-intercept of the line NQ is $\frac{4}{3}$,
 then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Let $P = (3t^{2}$
 , 6t) ; $N = (3t^{2}$
, 0)

$M = (3t^{2}$
, 3t)

Let point Q = (h, 3t) which lies on the parabola $y^{2} = 12x$

$\therefore$ $9t^{2} = 12h$

$\Rightarrow$ h = $\frac{3t^{2}}{4}$

Equation of NQ

y - 0 = $\frac{3t}{\frac{3t2}{4}-3t^{2}}\left (x-3t^{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ y = $\frac{-4}{3t}\left (x-3t^{2}\right )$

For y-intercept of NQ, x = 0

$\therefore$ y = 4t

Given y-intercept of the line NQ is $\frac{4}{3}$

$\therefore$ 4t = $\frac{4}{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ t = $\frac{1}{3}$

$\therefore$ MQ = $\frac{9t^{2}}{4}$ = $\frac{1}{4}$

PN = 6t = 2

text:
Consider the two sets :

A = {m $\in$ R : both the roots of
 $x^{2}$
 – (m + 1)x + m + 4 = 0 are real} 

and B = [–3, 5).

Which of the following is not true?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As roots are real so, $D\geq 0$

$(m+1)^{2}-4(m+4)\geq 0$

$\Rightarrow m^{2}-2m-15\geq 0$

$\Rightarrow$ $(m-5)(m+3)\geq 0$

$m\in \qquad$($-\infty$, $-$3] $\cup$ [5, $\infty$)

$A=(-\infty$, $-$3] $\cup$ [5, $\infty$)

Given B = [$-$3, 5)
Now, let's examine the options.

Option A : A ∩ B = {–3}
The intersection of sets A and B would be the set of elements common to both sets. In this case, the only common element is -3. So, option A is true.

Option B : B – A = (–3, 5)
The subtraction (or difference) of sets A from B is the set of elements that are in B but not in A. B is [–3, 5), and A is (-∞, -3] U [5, ∞). Subtracting A from B would leave an open interval (-3, 5), not including -3 and 5. So, option B is also true.

Option C : A ∪ B = R
The union of sets A and B is the set of elements that are in A, or B, or both. Here, A U B would cover all real numbers. So, option C is true.

Option D : A - B = (-∞, -3) ∪ (5, ∞)
The subtraction (or difference) of set B from A is the set of elements that are in A but not in B. B is [–3, 5), and A is (-∞, -3] U [5, ∞). Subtracting B from A would leave (-∞, -3) U [5, ∞), which contains 5 (5 is in A but not in B), so it is not (-∞, -3) ∪ (5, ∞). So, option D is not true.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
If $y^{2} + \log _{e} (\cos ^{2}x) = y$, 
$x\in \left (-\frac{π}{2},\frac{π}{2}\right )$, then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $y^{2} + \log _{e} (\cos ^{2}x) = y .....(1)$

Put x  = 0, we get

$y^{2} + \log _{e} (1) = y$

$\Rightarrow$ $y^{2} = y$

$\Rightarrow$ y = 0, 1

Differentiating (1) we get

2yy' + $\frac{2}{\cos x}(-\sin x)$ = y'

$\Rightarrow$ 2yy' - 2tanx = y'  ....(2)

From (2) when x = 0, y = 0 then y'(0) = 0

From (2) when x = 0, y = 1 then 

2y' = y'

$\Rightarrow$ y'(0) = 0

Again differentiating (2) we get

$2(y')^{2}$
 $+ 2yy'' – 2\sec ^{2}x = y''$

from (2) when x = 0, y = 0, y’(0) = 0 then

y”(0) = -2

Also from (2) when x = 0, y = 1, y’(0) = 0 then

y”(0) = 2

$\therefore$ |y''(0)| = 2

text:
The solution curve of the differential equation,

$(1 + e^{-x})(1 + y^{2})\frac{dy}{dx}$ $= y^{2}$,

which passes through
the point (0, 1), is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $(1 + e^{-x})(1 + y^{2})\frac{dy}{dx}$ $= y^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (\frac{y^{2}+1}{y^{2}}\right )dy=\frac{e^{x}dx}{e^{x}+1}$

Integrating both sides,

$\int \left (\frac{y^{2}+1}{y^{2}}\right )dy=\int \frac{e^{x}dx}{e^{x}+1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $y-\frac{1}{y}=\ln |e^{x}+1|+c$

It passes through (0, 1)

$\Rightarrow$ c = $-\ln 2$

$\Rightarrow$ $y^{2}-1=yln\left (\frac{e^{x}+1}{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $y^{2}=1+yln\left (\frac{e^{x}+1}{2}\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
If the number of integral terms in the expansion

of $(3^{1/2} + 5^{1/8})^{n}$ is exactly 33, then the least value
of n is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
General term of the expression,

$T_{r+1}={}^{n}C_{r}\left (3^{\frac{1}{2}}\right )^{n-r}\left (5^{\frac{1}{8}}\right )^{r}$

$={}^{n}C_{r}(3)^{\frac{n-r}{2}}(5)^{\frac{r}{8}}$

We will get integral term when $\frac{n-r}{2}$ and $\frac{r}{8}$ are integer

$\therefore$ (1) n $-$ r is multiple of 2

$\Rightarrow$ n $-$ r = 0, 2, 4, ......

(2) r is multiple of 8

$\Rightarrow$ r = 0, 8, 16, .......

From this two conditions common values are = 0, 8, 16, ....... which will becomes integral terms.

Given that there are 33 integral terms.

Here first integral term at $0^{th}$ position.

Second integral term at $8^{th}$ position.

$\therefore$ $33^{th}$ integral term will be at = 0 + (33 $-$ 1)8 = 256

So, there should be at least 256 terms.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
If $α$ and $β$ are the roots of the equation

$x^{2}$
 + px + 2 = 0 and $\frac{1}{α}$ and $\frac{1}{β}$ are the
 roots of
the equation $2x^{2}$
 + 2qx + 1 = 0, then

$\left (α-\frac{1}{α}\right )\left (β-\frac{1}{β}\right )\left (α+\frac{1}{β}\right )\left (β+\frac{1}{α}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$α$ and $β$ are the roots of the 

equation
$x^{2}$
 + px + 2 = 0

$\therefore$ $α+β=-p,αβ=2$

$\frac{1}{α}$ and $\frac{1}{β}$ are the roots of
the 

equation $2x^{2}$
 + 2qx + 1 = 0

$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{α}+\frac{1}{β}=-q,\frac{1}{αβ}=\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{α+β}{αβ}=-q\Rightarrow \frac{-p}{2}=-q$

$\Rightarrow p=2q$

$\left (α+\frac{1}{β}\right )\left (β+\frac{1}{α}\right )=αβ+\frac{1}{αβ}+2$ $=2+\frac{1}{2}+2=\frac{9}{2}$

$\left (α-\frac{1}{α}\right )\left (β-\frac{1}{β}\right )=αβ+\frac{1}{αβ}-\frac{α}{β}-\frac{β}{α}$

$=2+\frac{1}{2}-\left [\frac{α^{2}+β^{2}}{αβ}\right ]=\frac{5}{2}-\left [\frac{(α+β)^{2}-2αβ}{αβ}\right ]$

$=\frac{5}{2}-\left [\frac{p^{2}-4}{2}\right ]$

$=\frac{9-p^{2}}{2}$

$\left (α-\frac{1}{α}\right )\left (β-\frac{1}{β}\right )\left (α+\frac{1}{β}\right )\left (β+\frac{1}{α}\right )=\left (\frac{9-p^{2}}{2}\right )\left (\frac{9}{2}\right )$

$=\frac{9}{4}(9-p^{2})$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
Let [t] denote the greatest integer
$\leq$ t. If for some

$λ$ $\in$ R - {1, 0}, $\lim _{x\to 0}\left |\frac{1-x+|x|}{λ-x+[x]}\right |$ = L, then L is
equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Here $\lim _{x\to 0}\left |\frac{1-x+|x|}{λ-x+[x]}\right |=L$

Here L.H.L. $\lim _{h\to 0^{-}}\left |\frac{1+h+h}{λ+h-1}\right |=\left |\frac{1}{λ-1}\right |$

R.H.L. = $\lim _{h\to 0^{+}}\left |\frac{1-h+h}{λ-h+0}\right |=\left |\frac{1}{λ}\right |$

$\because$ Limit exists. Hence L.H.L. = R.H.L.

$\Rightarrow$ $|λ-1|=|λ|$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ=\frac{1}{2}$ 

$\therefore$ L = $\frac{1}{|λ|}$ = 2
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
Let A = $\left [\begin{array}{ll} x & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{array}\right ]$, x $\in$ R and $A^{4} =$ [$a_{ij}$].

If
$a_{11} = 109$, then $a_{22}$ is equal to $_______$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A^{2}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} x & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{ll} x & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} x^{2}+1 & x \\ x & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

$A^{4}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} x^{2}+1 & x \\ x & 1 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{ll} x^{2}+1 & x \\ x & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

$=\left [\begin{array}{ll} (x^{2}+1)^{2}+x^{2} & x(x^{2}+1)+x \\ x(x^{2}+1)+x & x^{2}+1 \end{array}\right ]$

Given $(x^{2}+1)^{2}+x^{2}=109$

Let $x^{2}+1$ = t

$t^{2}+t-1=109$

$\Rightarrow$ (t $-$ 10) (t + 11) = 0

$\therefore$ $t = 10 = x^{2} + 1 = a_{22}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
If $\lim _{x\to 0}\left \{\frac{1}{x^{8}}\left (1-\cos \frac{x^{2}}{2}-\cos \frac{x^{2}}{4}+\cos \frac{x^{2}}{2}\cos \frac{x^{2}}{4}\right )\right \}$ $= 2^{-k}$

then the value of k is $_______$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to 0}\left \{\frac{1}{x^{8}}\left (1-\cos \frac{x^{2}}{2}-\cos \frac{x^{2}}{4}+\cos \frac{x^{2}}{2}\cos \frac{x^{2}}{4}\right )\right \}=2^{-k}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{\left (1-\cos \frac{x2}{2}\right )}{4\left (\frac{x2}{2}\right )^{2}}\frac{\left (1-\cos \frac{x2}{4}\right )}{16\left (\frac{x2}{4}\right )^{2}}$ = $2^{-k}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{2\sin ^{2}\frac{x2}{4}}{16\left (\frac{x2}{4}\right )^{2}}\times \frac{2\sin ^{2}\frac{x2}{8}}{64\left (\frac{x2}{8}\right )^{2}}$ $= 2^{-k}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{8}\times \frac{1}{32}=2^{-k}$

$\Rightarrow$ $2^{-8} = 2^{-k}$ 

$\Rightarrow$ k = 8
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
The diameter of the circle, whose centre lies on
the line x + y = 2 in the first quadrant and which
touches both the lines x = 3 and y = 2, is
$_______$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$\because$ center lies on x + y = 2 and in $1^{st}$ quadrant center = ($α$, 2 $-$ $α$)

where $α$ > 0 and 2 $-$ $α$ > 0 $\Rightarrow$ 0 < $α$ < 2

$\because$ circle touches x = 3 and y = 2

$\therefore$ $\frac{|α-3|}{1}=r$

and $\frac{|2-(2-α)|}{1}=r$

$\Rightarrow \quad |α|=r$

$\therefore$ $|α-3|=|α|$

$\Rightarrow$ $α^{2}-6α+9=α^{2}$

$\Rightarrow α=\frac{3}{2}$

$\therefore$ $r=\frac{3}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ 2r = 3 = diameter.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text: The value of $(0.16)^{\log _{2.5}\left (\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3 2}+....to\infty \right )}$ is equal to $______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $(0.16)^{\log _{2.5}\left (\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3 2}+....to\infty \right )}$

As sum of GP upto infinity = $\frac{a}{1-r}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3^{2}}+\frac{1}{3^{3}}+....\infty$ = $\frac{\frac{1}{3}}{1-\frac{1}{3}}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$

$\therefore$ $(0.16)^{\log _{2.5}\left (\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3 2}+....to\infty \right )}$

= $(0.16)^{\log _{2.5}\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )}$

= $\left (\frac{16}{100}\right )^{\log _{2.5}\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )}$

= $\left (\frac{4}{10}\right )^{\log _{2.5}\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )}$

= $\left [\left (\frac{10}{4}\right )^{-2}\right ]^{\log _{2.5}\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )}$

= $\left [(2.5)^{-2}\right ]^{\log _{2.5}\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )}$

= $(2.5)^{-2\log _{2.5}\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )}$

= $\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )^{-2}$ = 4
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot

text:
If $\left (\frac{1+i}{1-i}\right )^{\frac{m}{2}}=\left (\frac{1+i}{i-1}\right )^{\frac{n}{3}}=1$, (m, n
$\in$ N) then the
greatest common divisor of the least values of
m and n is $_______$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left (\frac{1+i}{1-i}\right )^{m/2}=\left (\frac{1+i}{i-1}\right )^{n/3}=1$

$\Rightarrow \left (\frac{(1+i)^{2}}{2}\right )^{m/2}=\left (\frac{(1+i)^{2}}{-2}\right )^{n/3}=1$

$\Rightarrow (i)^{m/2}=(-i)^{n/3}=1$ $= i^{4}$ [ As $i^{4} = 1$]

$\Rightarrow \frac{m}{2}=4k_{1}and\frac{n}{3}=4k_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $m = 8 k_{1}$ and $n = 12 k_{2}$

Least value of m = 8 and n = 12.

$\therefore$ GCD (8, 12) = 4
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Morning Slot
